# Hopperlace

> Choose AI for what you want to do — and what matters to you.

We're building Hopperlace to help you compare what AI tools can do, what they're like to use, and how they fit your values.

Explore the values side today with ValueCompass. Comparisons of tool capabilities and experience are in development.

Focus: independent testing · comparison · informed choice.

## ValueCompass — available now (https://valuecompass.ai)

Explore the values behind your AI choices.

Who benefits from the money you spend on AI? What commitments do providers make to the people affected by their technology?

ValueCompass helps you examine the companies behind AI products and compare options against your values. Explore ownership, control and documented commitments, with sources and clear gaps in the research.

Opens valuecompass.ai. No account needed.

## What we're building — in development

Repeatable tests of AI tools on real tasks.

We're developing repeatable tests of AI tools, starting with AI app builders. Each comparison will use the same tasks across several tools, with multiple runs to examine how results vary. We'll combine automated tests with hands-on review to examine both the output and the experience of using each tool.

The aim is to bring these comparisons together with ValueCompass, so you can consider practical fit and values in the same decision.

What each comparison will examine:

1. Results — does the output do what the task asked?
2. Fixes — what errors occur, and how many attempts does it take to resolve them?
3. Time — time from the initial instructions to a usable result.
4. Cost — the cost of completing the task, including retries.
5. Assistance — the guidance and technical knowledge needed to reach a useful result.

Note: these are planned evaluation dimensions, not published results. No benchmark dataset or automated lab exists yet.

## How we approach a choice

Three questions worth asking of any AI tool.

1. Can it do the task? A tool's strengths need to match the work you want to do.
2. What is it like to use? The setup and effort involved need to suit your skills and how you work.
3. Does it fit what matters to you? Your choice also supports the companies behind the tools, with their ownership, practices and commitments.

## Founder

Hopperlace was founded by Yuyu Shen, a statistically trained data scientist turned product manager with nearly a decade building and evaluating AI systems, including taking AI products from zero to one.

She also built Evidence Synthesis AI (https://www.evidencesynthesisai.com/), a tool for screening research literature that refers uncertain cases to human reviewers. Her research on deference-aware evaluation was accepted at the ICML 2026 Technical AI Governance workshop. She holds CCA-F and CCA-P certifications and writes about technology, agency and better decisions at https://buildwithwhy.com.

### Deference-Aware Evaluation for Human-in-the-Loop AI Systems
- Author: Yuyu Shen
- Date: 2026
- DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/A69YH
- Link: https://osf.io/a69yh/
- Venue: Technical AI Governance workshop, ICML 2026

## Services (https://hopperlace.ai/services)

Need help choosing an AI tool or testing an idea?

Hopperlace works with teams to understand a workflow, compare options and test promising approaches. You get findings and a recommendation to help you decide what to use, what to build, or what to investigate next.

How it works:

1. Understand — establish how the workflow operates today and what a better outcome would mean for your customers or business.
2. Compare and test — test promising approaches on your tasks, building a prototype where useful.
3. Explain and recommend — present the findings, trade-offs and recommended next steps.

Questions this suits:

- "Which of these AI tools should our team use for this work?"
- "Is this model good enough for our use case, and how would we know?"
- "Should we build this ourselves, buy it, or wait?"
- "A vendor is claiming this works. Can we check before we sign?"

What you get: projects end with findings, a recommendation and any agreed prototype or evaluation materials. Implementation and ongoing delivery remain with your team. You can reuse the evaluation tasks and criteria when your needs or the available tools change.
